title: Treatment of coagulopathy in COVID-19 patients: protocol for a scoping review
author: Hirotaka Mori
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgrpjv5n

steps.title: Define Research Question and Inclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the research question and define the Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework for study inclusion.

substeps.instruction: Set research question: 'What anticoagulants were or will be used to treat DIC or coagulopathy in COVID-19 patients'

Define Population: COVID-19 patients with coagulopathy assessed by ISTH DIC score, JAAM DIC score, JMHW DIC score, JSTH DIC score, sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) score, or laboratory coagulation tests; patients must have received any anticoagulants.
Define Concept: Review existing literature on treatment and prognosis of coagulopathy in COVID-19 patients.
Define Context: No limits on geographic location, race, gender, or healthcare setting.

Apply exclusion criteria: Exclude studies not reporting prognosis, patients receiving anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism or other diseases, patients with coagulopathy after recovering from COVID-19, or pregnant patients.

steps.title: Perform Systematic Literature Search
steps.instruction: Execute a three-step search strategy to identify relevant studies registered until 21 May 2020.

substeps.instruction: Step 1: Conduct an initial limited search of MEDLINE, analyzing titles, abstracts, and index terms.

Step 2: Search MEDLINE, CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO-ICTRP), and PROSPERO using specific search strings for 'disseminated intravascular coagulation', 'coagulopathy', 'anticoagulants', 'coronavirus', and 'COVID'.
Step 3: Check the reference lists of all included studies for additional resources.

steps.title: Select Studies
steps.instruction: Screen identified studies using the PRISMA flow diagram and predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Perform independent screening of titles and abstracts by two researchers (HM and HO).
Resolve disagreements through discussion.
Conduct pilot testing using a random sample of 50 citations; if agreement is <75%, modify eligibility criteria.
Document and report reasons for excluded studies.

steps.title: Chart Study Data
steps.instruction: Extract and map data from included studies into a structured table (Map 1), ordered by publication year.

substeps.instruction: Chart study design (case report, case series, case-controlled, retrospective/prospective cohort, or RCT).
Chart coagulopathy assessment (ISTH, JAAM, JMHW, JSTH, SIC scores, or tests like D-dimer).
Chart severity (scoring system or ICU need).
Chart anticoagulants used (prophylactic/therapeutic doses of unfractionated heparin, prophylactic/therapeutic doses of low molecular weight heparin, recombinant thrombomodulin, etc.).
Chart outcomes (mortality, DIC, venous thromboembolism, multiple organ failure, coagulation laboratory data, or side effects).
Conduct pilot testing using a random 50% sample of included studies; if agreement is <75%, modify charting data.
Use symbols for the map: ● (data described/used), ? (insufficient information), and blank (data not used).

steps.title: Collate, Summarize, and Report Results
steps.instruction: Synthesize the extracted data and report findings according to PRISMA guidelines for scoping reviews.

substeps.instruction: Present search results using the PRISMA flow chart.
Organize extracted data into a map, diagrammatic form, table, and descriptive format.
Describe any methodological changes made during the study in the results section.
Prepare the final publication for peer-reviewed journals.

description:
2 Background Coronavirus infection disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients have a significant association with coagulopathy. Development of coagulopathy is triggered by inflammation cytokines especially in the case of infection (Walborn et al., 2018). In addition to this basic mechanism, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infects endothelial cells. SARS-CoV-2 exploits the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor and induce diffuse endothelial inflammation(Varga et al., 2020) resulting in thrombotic microangiopathies (Gavriilaki and Brodsky, 2020). This complex process is the characteristic coagulopathy aggravated by SARS-CoV-2. A previous observational study showed that abnormal coagulation results, especially markedly elevated D-dimer and the presence of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) were frequently noted in deaths with COVID-
19 patients (Tang et al., 2020). Generally, the control of coagulopathy using anticoagulants and the treatment of underlying disease is the primary concern. Anticoagulants including unfractionated heparin, low-molecular-weight heparin or recombinant thrombomodulin have shown the effectiveness (Murao and Yamakawa, 2019) and are recommended (Wada et al., 2013). Although the evidence of the treatment of coagulopathy in COVID-19 patients is compiling(Thachil et al., 2020), there is no scoping review on this topic to our knowledge. The objective of this scoping review is to systematically map the anticoagulants used in this area and to identify the existing gaps between investigated anticoagulants and not. Methods In preparing this protocol manuscript, the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-
ScR) (Tricco et al., 2018) statement was used.
